**About 12.8% of Alberta children under 18 were in poverty in 2024**, the latest year available. This uses the Market Basket Measure (MBM), Canada's official poverty line, on its 2023 base.

- **Source:** Statistics Canada, Table 11-10-0135-01, vector v1792632015 (Alberta, persons under 18, MBM 2023 base, percentage in low income).
- **Reference period:** calendar year 2024. Statistics Canada rates the estimate quality "C" (good).
- **Recent trend (same vector):** 4.6% in 2020, 8.1% in 2021, 12.0% in 2022, 11.9% in 2023 and 12.8% in 2024.
- **Older MBM base:** the 2018-base series (v1206133320) gives 11.7% for 2023, close to the 11.9% on the 2023 base. It ends in 2023.

The rate depends on which low-income line you use. Table 11-10-0135-01 also has the after-tax Low Income Measure and the Low Income Cut-offs, which would give different figures. I didn't pull those.

Average weekly earnings for all employees in Alberta's provincial and territorial public administration, including overtime, were **$1,877.58** in July 2026. That is the latest month available. It was $1,667.49 in July 2025, a rise of about 12.6%.
